title: Round 24 Southern Plains state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Oklahoma and Texas. Every seeded row reproduces one accepted USGS GNIS Geocoder candidate screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned primary point. Guadalupe Peak additionally carries a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check; the Red River returned record was reviewed per-ID and rejected for the intended feature.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Political divisions, counties, colonias, channels, historical air fields, airports, branches, bayous, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Per-ID identity checks for Guadalupe Peak (1358489), confirming the Texas High Point description and variant names, and for the rejected Red River record (1344947), whose coordinate sequences sit in Brown County rather than the intended Texas-Oklahoma border reach.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes, Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records, Bays & Harbors to Bay, Valley to Valley, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline or bay polygon, canyon rim, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, or the returned record does not identify the intended feature, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors plus one labelled generalized Gulf coast line for Texas; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

oklahoma.title: Oklahoma statewide frame
oklahoma.frameNote: Southern Plains batch: the Oklahoma City, Tulsa, and Lawton anchors are balanced with Mount Scott, the Texoma/Grand Lake/Tenkiller reservoirs, and the Canadian/Illinois river records. identityDecisions.decision: Seeded after a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check confirmed Class=Summit, Primary State=Texas, Primary County=Culberson County, coordinate sequence 1 at the stored point marked High Point, the description Highest elevation in TX at 8749 feet in Guadalupe Mountains National Park, and a January 1 1936 Board decision; the Geocoder returned a single exact Summit record and the coordinate matches.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The primary point is not a surveyed boundary of the Guadalupe Mountains or the park. The per-ID variant names El Capitan Peak, Signal Peak, and Guadaloupe Peak (misspelled) are variants of this same record, not separate features, and are not seeded as rows.

identityDecisions.decision: No row seeded. The exact-name states=OK Geocoder screens returned empty arrays twice on 2026-10-23 (maxSuggestions 10 and 25).
identityDecisions.reason: An empty screen for the intended exact record stays unseeded under the round-20/21/22/23 rule; no substitute feature is promoted to high point. Mount Scott is seeded as a Wichita Mountains summit and its note states it is not the state high point.

identityDecisions.candidate: Red River: states=OK screen empty; states=TX stream record 1344947 reviewed per-ID
identityDecisions.decision: No Red River row seeded in either frame; generalized border corridor only.
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: The states=TX screen returned an exact-name Stream record, but the per-ID check shows Primary State=Texas, Primary County=Brown County, and coordinate sequences 1 and 2 near 31.95 N / 99.07 W in Brown County with no description. That record does not identify the intended Texas-Oklahoma border reach (roughly 34.4 N), so it was rejected rather than seeded; Red River County (1383979), Red River City (1377149), and Red River Army Depot (2511991) are further same-name rejections. Consistent with the round-22 Red River of the North empty screens in North Dakota.

identityDecisions.candidate: Arkansas River under states=OK; Gloss Mountains under states=OK
identityDecisions.decision: No gazetteer rows seeded; generalized context corridor for the Arkansas River.
identityDecisions.reason: Both exact-name state-filtered screens returned empty arrays. The Arkansas result is the third consecutive empty screen for the same intended stream after round-18 Colorado and round-23 Kansas.

knownLimitations: Oklahoma and Texas are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence, and the returned county is primary-county provenance. Guadalupe Peak additionally carries a per-ID Domestic Names detail check, and the Red River record was reviewed per-ID before rejection.

GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines; the Texas Gulf coast line is labelled generalized context, not a survey.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include small areas outside their state outlines, and the Texas rectangle also includes open Gulf area beyond the coast line; no boundary geometry is claimed.
